content.title: About
content.content: Toasted cinnamon bread consists of slices of bread toasted to a golden crisp and flavored with ground cinnamon. It offers a sweet‑spicy taste and a crunchy texture, making it perfect for breakfast or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cinnamon is one of the oldest spices, used in cooking for over 4,000 years.
Toasting intensifies the cinnamon aroma and gives the bread a satisfying crunch.
In many countries toasted cinnamon bread is served with butter or cream cheese.
The sweet spice combined with slightly bitter toasted bread creates a balanced flavor profile.
Toasted bread is often used in desserts such as French toast.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Bread provides a quick source of energy through complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions supply dietary fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants from cinnamon
items.content: Cinnamon is rich in polyphenols, which may help reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports blood sugar regulation
items.content: Some studies suggest cinnamon can improve insulin sensitivity.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing aroma
items.content: The scent of cinnamon is often linked to improved mood and reduced stress.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened versions may contain added sugar, which is unsuitable for diabetics.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional bread contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Toasted bread with butter and cinnamon can be calorie‑rich, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Excess cinnamon intake
items.content: Large amounts of cinnamon (especially cassia) may lead to excess coumarin, which can be harmful to the liver.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toast slices until golden, sprinkle with ground cinnamon, and optionally drizzle with honey or maple syrup. Serve with butter, cream cheese, or as a base for fruit toppings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bread in a cool, dry place in an airtight bag. Toasted slices are best consumed within 2–3 days, otherwise they may become soggy. For longer storage, freeze the slices and re‑toast before eating.
